name: Greenland
summary_text: Greenland: self-rule; Danish human-rights framework applies; comparatively tolerant Inuit communities; policing capacity is the weak link. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: Denmark (0.85) plus a local delta of -0.02. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: Denmark's decade of self-ID cools debate on trans rights | Context by TRF
sources.claim_summary: Context/Thomson Reuters Foundation (Sept 2024) on Denmark's decade of self-ID - included for Greenland as part of the Danish Realm; Greenland adopted its own gender-recognition framework based on self-declaration in 2016.

sources.title: Denmark | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview for Denmark (updated March 2026), included for Greenland as part of the Danish Realm: robust protections, self-determined gender markers, SOGISC discrimination protections.

sources.title: Gay Greenland--Past and Present - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz 'Gay Greenland - Past and Present' (May 2015): gay life in Greenland is 'almost a non-event' - low-key, integrated, non-violent; modest Pride march since 2010; the 1996 same-sex partnership law passed with virtually no debate - a picture of quiet tolerance.

sources.title: Gay Greenland--Past and Present - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz 'Gay Greenland - Past and Present' (alternate URL of the same May 2015 report): same content - no marriage-equality campaigns, no anti-gay clergy or politicians; same-sex partnership quietly passed in parliament.

sources.title: Same sex couples can now officially marry in Greenland | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (April 2016): Greenland's same-sex marriage law came into effect - adopted Danish legislation, passed unanimously twice (first bill lapsed due to Danish elections); replaces the 1996 Danish-derived partnership law; Bishop Sofie Petersen supported it.

sources.title: Ny landsforening for lesbiske, bøsser, bisexuelle og transkønnede | KNR
sources.claim_summary: KNR Greenlandic Broadcasting (Aug 2014, in Danish): new national association LGBT Qaamaneq founded for lesbians, gays, bisexuals and transgender people - aims for political, cultural and social equality; open to family, friends and colleagues as supporters.
